key_insight: HarmQ shows that quantum neural networks can be backdoored with harmonic, low-frequency triggers that survive downsampling and match the spectral bias of parameterized quantum circuits.
engineering_relevance: This reveals a practical security risk for NISQ-era quantum machine learning systems and suggests robustness testing must account for quantum-native trigger structures.
method: Inject sinusoidal perturbations on coarse grids
Use block-uniform patterns so triggers survive aggressive downsampling
Exploit PQC Fourier decomposition bias toward low-frequency components
evidence_signal: On MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, HarmQ reports over 99% attack success rate while preserving more than 90% clean accuracy, far outperforming prior attack baselines.
watch_item: The attack assumes the adversary can access training data, so deployment settings with stricter data control or preprocessing may reduce feasibility.
paper_title: HarmQ: Harmonic Backdoor Attacks Against Quantum Neural Networks
